memory_update.text: LYTS is the cleanest underfollowed US-listed small-cap candidate found for retail/QSR/grocery fixture and display exposure within the inventory_availability_components node.

GIC should be tracked as an availability-driven distributor candidate for storage, shelving, cabinets, material handling, and facility-supply exposure tied to warehouses and commercial/retail buildouts.

EML is a speculative shadow candidate: micro-cap engineered hardware/metal-products exposure is plausible, but direct retail, cabinet, enclosure, or warehouse-fixture linkage must be verified before promotion to later Serenity layers.

The node appears to split into two investable sub-lanes: engineered enclosure/cabinet manufacturers and availability/catalog distributors of storage, shelving, cabinets, fixtures, and facility components.

Several pure-play enclosure and shelving manufacturers are private or non-US-listed; US-listed exposure may require accepting indirect distributors, lighting/display companies, or broader electrical-infrastructure references.

node: Specialty enclosures, cabinets, fixtures, displays, and availability-driven components for stores, warehouses, and job sites
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around availability-driven physical components used in retail remodels, grocery/QSR displays, warehouses, commercial buildouts, and job-site electrical infrastructure. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are not consumer-branded retailers, but distributors and niche manufacturers whose value may come from catalog breadth, inventory availability, engineered support, and customer-specific fixture or storage needs. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation.
